title: Ops Trust Lab: SLO experiment sprint notebook (Feb 2026)
content:
Purpose
This sprint notebook captures a focused, cross-functional experiment designed to validate a set of reliability controls and SLO tuning options for high-throughput model serving routes. Goal: reduce p99 tail latency for chat-generation routes by 15% without consuming >10% more GPU capacity and without regressing output quality.

Context & motivation
- Observations: several customer-facing services reported bursty p99 spikes tied to cold KV cache misses and occasional oversized batching decisions during mixed small/large sequence workloads.
- Risk drivers: unpredictable tail latency negatively affects SLAs for Dedicated customers and increases incident noise for oncall.
- Business impact: improving tail latency improves perceived product quality and reduces SLO burn; conservative tuning could also reduce unit cost by improving batching effectiveness.
- Hypothesis: a combined approach (adaptive prefix-KV warmup + short canary for small adaptive batch policy + targeted quantization-level fallback) will reduce p99 latency with acceptable capacity cost.

Scope
- Target services: generation-chat-route (model: redwood-v2-chat-0408-config), embeddings-batch-route (for small/large mix), and prefix-cache service (kv-cache cluster behind model-serving).
- In-scope experiments: 1) prefix-KV prewarming/proactive caching for recurring session keys, 2) adaptive batch-size limiter keyed by request token-length histogram, 3) a 5% canary of dynamic quantization fallback for long sequences.
- Out-of-scope: model architecture changes, network infra replacement, customer side timeouts.

Success criteria (decision gates)
- Primary metric: p99 latency for generation-chat-route (prod-like load): >=15% reduction sustained over a 7-day window in canary region.
- Cost constraint: sustained GPU cycle consumption increase <= 10% compared to baseline.
- Quality guardrail: automated evals on a curated prompt set (prompt-suite v3) show no statistically significant degradation in token-level similarity / response correctness (threshold: difference in evaluation score <= 0.02).
- Failure criteria: any sustained >2% increase in overall error rate (5xx or timeouts) or customer-visible L7 errors during canary.

Owners & stakeholders
- Experiment lead (SRE): Maya Chen — overall orchestration, runbook, metrics dashboard.
- Serving runtime engineer: Omar Ruiz — implement adaptive batching policy + coordination with runtime team for kernel selection telemetry.
- Applied ML / model onboard: Priya Singh — validate quantization fallback, evaluate quality on prompt-suite v3, maintain model-variant compatibility list.
- Platform infra: Liam O'Connor — prefix-cache autoscaler knobs and provisioning for warmup burst.
- Customer success stakeholder: Hannah Park — customer comms and monitoring for high-value customers during canary.
- Oncall backup: rotation assigned from SRE pager team during canary window.

Communications
- Pre-canary: post plan to #ops-trust-lab and #sre-ops-announce 48 hours prior. Tag TLs for Dedicated customers.
- During canary: hourly short-check updates in #ops-trust-lab, immediate pager escalation per runbook.
- Post-canary: 1-pager summary to product and sales, and a retro in the weekly SRE sync.

Experiment plan & timeline (6 weeks)
- Week 0 (preparation, 7 days): finalize measurement dashboards, load generator configs, and QA small-scale staging runs. Jira tickets: SRE-1423 (batching change), PLAT-2981 (kv-warmup flow). Owners: Maya, Omar, Liam.
- Week 1 (staging validations, 3 days): run full smoke, validate telemetry events (batch_size, kernel_choice, kv_hit_rate).
- Week 2 (canary rollout 1 - 2 regions, 5% traffic, 3 days): enable prefix-warmup and adaptive batching limiter (no quantization fallback yet). Measure p50/p95/p99, cost signals.
- Week 3 (analysis + iter, 4 days): adjust thresholds, prepare small-scale quantization variant for long sequences.
- Week 4 (canary rollout 2 - add 5% quantization fallback, total 10% traffic, 4 days): observe latency and quality. If quality regression exceeds guardrail, immediate rollback of quantization.
- Week 5 (extended monitoring + ramp decision, 7 days): decision checkpoint — promote to 25% if success criteria met, or abort/iterate.
- Week 6 (retrospective & next steps): retro notes, production rollout plan, runbooks and operational docs.

Measurement plan & dashboards
- Primary dashboards (Grafana): route_p99_latency, route_p95, kv_cache_hit_rate, batch_size_distribution, gpu_utilization_by_pool, error_rate_5xx.
- Derived signals: SLO burn rate per minute, tail-latency contribution by kernel version, prefix-warmup hit ratio.
- Alerting adjustments: temporary canary alert thresholds will be used for non-actionable drift; only route error-rate/timeout alerts will page.

Runbook (quick summary)
- Canary start: record baseline snapshot (metrics and snapshots), enable feature flags for 5% traffic, monitor for 30 minutes with dedicated observer.
- If p99 increases >5% above baseline without improvement in 30 minutes: pause ramp and revert batching change.
- If error-rate or timeouts cross failure criteria: immediate rollback of last change and page oncall.
- If GPU utilization exceeds +10% sustained for 15 minutes: engage Liam for autoscaler tuning and consider reducing canary traffic.

Risk matrix & mitigation
- Risk: Quality regression from quantization fallback. Mitigation: run offline evals (Priya) and keep fallback rate at 5% initial; immediate rollback if eval fails.
- Risk: Increased cost from prefix-warmup. Mitigation: TTL limits, heatmap-based warmup only for top-3% session keys, daily budget cap for warmup population.
- Risk: Undetected edge-case that increases p50 for small sequences. Mitigation: include separate histogram splits by sequence length and isolate bump behavior per bin.

Open questions for this sprint (to resolve in Week 0)
- What is the approved budget headroom for warmup traffic in Dedicated customer clusters? (need product confirmation)
- Should we expose warmup opt-out to high-sensitivity customers during canary? (customer success input)
- Exact acceptance thresholds for model-variant fallback quality (Priya to propose numeric thresholds).

Artifacts & links
- Load generator config: https://gh.redwood.ai/infra/loadgen/blob/ops-trust/warmup-config.yaml (PR forthcoming).
- Jira tickets: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SRE-1423, https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PLAT-2981.
- Confluence: experiment playbook draft https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SRE/pages/12345.

Post-sprint deliverables
- Decision memo summarizing canary results and recommended production rollout strategy.
- Runbook additions for prefix-cache maintenance and warmup budget controls.
- One-pager for sales & CS describing expected customer impact and optional opt-out path.

Notes & scratchpad
- Quick wins to try in staging: increase kv-cache LRU window for hot-session keys; instrument batch-size telemetry with request-token-length tag.
- Priya: prepare blind eval set from recent production prompts (anonymized) to evaluate fallback.
- Omar: add fine-grained logging for kernel selection to correlate p99 spikes with kernel changes.

Prepared by: Maya Chen (experiment lead)
Reviewed: Omar Ruiz, Priya Singh, Liam O'Connor, Hannah Park

Next steps (immediately):
- Finalize the experiment feature-flag names and targeted route identifiers (Maya, today).
- Schedule pre-canary stake-holder review (48 hours before canary start) (Maya/Hannah).
- Ship staging PRs for adaptive batching and warmup flow (Omar/Liam)
